# A measurement, not a marketing claim

> Lead Green is a Katonic project on the energy behind AI tokens. Who runs it, who pays and what they gain, the publisher and how to reach the editor.
>
> Lead Green, a Katonic project. Canonical page: https://leadgreen.ai/about/ (this file: https://leadgreen.ai/about/index.md). Updated 19 October 2026, data version 2026-10-19. Licence: CC BY 4.0 for the compilation and text; sources keep their own licences. GPU energy only, measured at steady state on a busy server (the most energy-efficient configuration under a latency limit). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted. Every figure is a floor; a lightly used server sits well above it. Machine-readable data: https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/ (see llms.txt).

*About*

Lead Green exists to put one number in front of the people who buy, run and audit AI: the GPU energy it takes to serve a million tokens. It publishes the public measurements in one unit, explains what they mean, exposes them to software, and adds measurements of its own as they are made.

Cite this page: Lead Green, a Katonic project. About. https://leadgreen.ai/about/, release 2026-10-19, retrieved [date]. CC BY 4.0.

*Who runs it*

## A Katonic project

Lead Green is run by [Katonic](https://www.katonic.ai), a company that builds a sovereign AI platform for enterprises, telcos and governments. Katonic meets the energy question on every on-premise deployment: a fixed power feed, a fixed GPU count, and a customer who wants to know how many tokens that buys. The index started as the answer the team wished existed.

Lead Green is not a separate company and not a product. It is a project with an editor, a method and a change record.

*Publisher*

## Who publishes it, and how to reach them

- **Publisher.** Katonic AI Technology Ltd, a company registered in the Dubai International Financial Centre, registration CL9944. Registered office: Unit IH-00-VZ-01-FL-194, Level 1, Innovation Hub, Dubai International Financial Centre, Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Jurisdiction: Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC), United Arab Emirates.
- **Corrections, contributions and data requests.** [hello@leadgreen.ai](mailto:hello@leadgreen.ai), answered within ten working days.
- **Cite as.** Lead Green, Green Tokens index, release 2026-10-19, Katonic, https://leadgreen.ai/index/, retrieved [date]. The full block is on [the index](https://leadgreen.ai/index/#cite).
- **Archive.** Every dated release of the API is kept unchanged at `https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/releases/<date>/`, with a zip of the whole release, so a citation can be reproduced after the index changes. The list is [`releases/index.json`](https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/releases/index.json).

*Independence*

## Who pays, and what they gain

Lead Green is run and paid for by Katonic, which sells a sovereign AI platform and benefits when buyers ask the questions on this site. It takes no money from hardware, cloud or model vendors.

- **Funding.** Katonic pays for the site and the editor's time. Katonic sells an AI platform for on-premise and sovereign deployments. Weigh that when the site argues for consolidation or for measuring your own cluster.
- **Public or reproducible only.** Every figure comes from a public measurement or a manufacturer's specification, dated, linked and snapshotted, or from a Lead Green measurement published with its protocol and logs.
- **No money from other vendors.** Lead Green takes no sponsorship, advertising or paid placement from hardware, cloud or model vendors.
- **Katonic gets no special treatment.** Nothing on the site claims that the Katonic platform measures energy per token until it does, and when Katonic publishes a measurement of its own it is labelled as Katonic's, with the same protocol and review as anyone else's. Any row Katonic measures is checked by a named reviewer with no Katonic affiliation, to be named here before the first Katonic row is published.
- **Corrections in the open.** Errors are fixed on the page and recorded on the index's change list. Tell us and we will look.
- **No superlatives.** The word "green" in the name is a direction, not a verdict. The site does not rank anyone as green.

*In a tender*

## Using the index in a tender

Every figure on the index is public and reproducible from the source files linked in the sources ledger; Lead Green holds no data that is not on the page. If Katonic is a bidder in a tender that cites the index, cite the ML.ENERGY rows directly, use the compilation only for convenience, and disclose it. Suggested wording: "Floor values are taken from the ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (The ML.ENERGY Initiative; Apache 2.0 per the ml-energy/benchmark-v3 dataset card) as compiled by Lead Green, a Katonic project (leadgreen.ai, CC BY 4.0, retrieved [date]). Katonic is a potential bidder; the evaluation panel has recomputed the values from the primary source and the scoring method does not depend on Lead Green." Katonic's own bids are held to the same clause and the same floor as anyone else's.

While Katonic is a bidder in a tender that cites the index, rows change only when a source publishes a dated release. Tenders cite a dated release, kept at `https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/releases/<date>/`, so no later change can move a cited figure.

# Llama 3.1 8B Instruct: GPU energy per million output tokens

> GPU watt-hours per million output tokens for Llama 3.1 8B Instruct: 20 measured configurations, load curve and carbon by grid. From ML.ENERGY v3.0.
>
> Lead Green, a Katonic project. Canonical page: https://leadgreen.ai/models/llama-3-1-8b-instruct/ (this file: https://leadgreen.ai/models/llama-3-1-8b-instruct/index.md). Updated 19 October 2026, data version 2026-10-19. Licence: CC BY 4.0 for the compilation and text; sources keep their own licences. GPU energy only, measured at steady state on a busy server (the most energy-efficient configuration under a latency limit). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted. Every figure is a floor; a lightly used server sits well above it. Machine-readable data: https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/ (see llms.txt).

*[Models](https://leadgreen.ai/models/) · B200 and H100*

Llama 3.1 8B Instruct serves a million output tokens for **13.0 Wh/M** on 1 × B200 (running batch 2,043, median inter-token latency 125 ms) and **19.5 Wh/M** on 1 × H100 (running batch 511, median inter-token latency 47 ms), GPU energy only, at the most energy-efficient configuration the ML.ENERGY Leaderboard measured. That is the floor: a lightly loaded server sits above it.

**Model** [meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), a dense transformer, weights in BF16. **Measured** 20 configurations on B200 and H100. **Data** [models/llama-3-1-8b-instruct.json](https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/models/llama-3-1-8b-instruct.json). Updated 19 October 2026.

Cite this page: Lead Green, a Katonic project. Llama 3.1 8B Instruct: energy per million output tokens. https://leadgreen.ai/models/llama-3-1-8b-instruct/, release 2026-10-19, retrieved [date]. CC BY 4.0.

- [Every configuration](https://leadgreen.ai/models/llama-3-1-8b-instruct/#configurations)
- [Two generations](https://leadgreen.ai/models/llama-3-1-8b-instruct/#generations)
- [Carbon](https://leadgreen.ai/models/llama-3-1-8b-instruct/#carbon)
- [Questions](https://leadgreen.ai/models/llama-3-1-8b-instruct/#faq)
- [Sources](https://leadgreen.ai/models/llama-3-1-8b-instruct/#sources)

- **Index row, B200:** 13.0 Wh/M 1 × B200, BF16. Running batch 2,043, median ITL 125 ms, 691 W across the cards, 14,799 tokens a second.
- **Index row, H100:** 19.5 Wh/M 1 × H100, BF16. Running batch 511, median ITL 47 ms, 688 W across the cards, 9,806 tokens a second.

GPU only, busy server. Every row is a floor. The number a buyer should ask for is the one measured on their own server at their own load. Unit: watt-hours per million output tokens (Wh/M); one Wh/M is 0.0036 joules per token.

*Every configuration*

## Llama 3.1 8B Instruct at every measured load

On 1 × H100, Llama 3.1 8B Instruct runs from **126.3 Wh/M** at a running batch of 8 to **19.5 Wh/M** at 511, a fall of 6.5×, while the cards' draw rises 41 percent (from 486 to 688 W) and throughput rises 9.2× (from 1,070 to 9,806 tokens a second). Median inter-token latency stays at 47 ms or under up to the best row. Past it, at a cap of 768, the same cards read 19.8 Wh/M at 63 ms.

*Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, BF16, 1 × B200: nine measured configurations*

| Cap | Running batch (avg) | Wh / M | Median ITL (ms) | Tokens / s | GPU power (W) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 8 | 108.5 | 5 | 1,637 | 639 |
| 16 | 16 | 67.3 | 5 | 2,751 | 667 |
| 32 | 32 | 42.0 | 6 | 3,810 | 576 |
| 64 | 64 | 30.6 | 9 | 5,589 | 617 |
| 128 | 128 | 27.3 | 27 | 4,570 | 449 |
| 256 | 255 | 19.6 | 32 | 7,664 | 540 |
| 512 | 511 | 16.7 | 50 | 9,571 | 577 |
| 1,024 | 1,021 | 15.3 | 87 | 10,922 | 600 |
| 2,048 | 2,043 | 13.0 | 125 | 14,799 | 691 |

*Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, BF16, 1 × H100: eleven measured configurations*

| Cap | Running batch (avg) | Wh / M | Median ITL (ms) | Tokens / s | GPU power (W) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 8 | 126.3 | 7 | 1,070 | 486 |
| 16 | 16 | 73.0 | 8 | 1,954 | 513 |
| 32 | 32 | 45.8 | 9 | 3,391 | 560 |
| 64 | 64 | 32.9 | 12 | 5,147 | 610 |
| 96 | 96 | 28.6 | 14 | 6,260 | 644 |
| 128 | 128 | 26.4 | 16 | 7,037 | 669 |
| 192 | 192 | 23.2 | 21 | 8,223 | 688 |
| 256 | 255 | 21.3 | 26 | 9,010 | 691 |
| 384 | 383 | 20.6 | 38 | 9,248 | 687 |
| 512 | 511 | 19.5 | 47 | 9,806 | 688 |
| 768 | 691 | 19.8 | 63 | 9,603 | 685 |

Cap is the configured maximum batch (vLLM's `max_num_seqs`). Running batch (avg) is the average number of requests the server was decoding at once over the steady-state window (vLLM's `num_requests_running`); queued requests are not counted. The highlighted row is the index row for that GPU. Wh/M is derived from the source's joules per output token; prompt processing is included.

*Two generations*

## H100 against B200

On the index rows, the H100 configuration uses 1.50× the energy per token of the B200 configuration: 19.5 Wh/M on 1 × H100 against 13.0 Wh/M on 1 × B200. The two rows were not swept alike: the H100 row holds a running batch of 511 on 1 card and the B200 row 2,043 on 1, so part of the gap is the sweep, not the silicon. The full comparison across 14 models is on [the index](https://leadgreen.ai/index/#generations).

*Carbon*

## Same tokens, different grid

A billion output tokens of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct on 1 × B200 at its index row carries about 8.9 kg CO2e of GPU-side emissions on the Saudi grid (689 gCO2e per kWh, Ember 2024) and 0.4 kg on the Norwegian grid (30). Energy per token does not change with geography; carbon per token does.

*Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, 1 × B200 index row (13.0 Wh/M), priced on 2024 annual grid averages, location-based*

| Grid | g CO2e per kWh | kg CO2e per billion output tokens |
|---|---|---|
| India | 707 | 9.2 |
| Saudi Arabia | 689 | 8.9 |
| Hong Kong | 676 | 8.8 |
| Serbia | 668 | 8.7 |
| World | 473 | 6.1 |
| Germany | 340 | 4.4 |
| Norway | 30 | 0.4 |

Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000. Lifecycle emissions intensity: CO2e per kWh of net generation, built from per-technology lifecycle factors (IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III midpoints, all gases at GWP-100), so upstream methane, supply chains and plant manufacture are included. Production-based: imports and grid losses are excluded. A location-based figure for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported. All 193 grids are in [grid.json](https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/grid.json); the [MCP server](https://leadgreen.ai/mcp/) prices any model on any grid.

*Questions*

## Asked about Llama 3.1 8B Instruct

### How much energy does Llama 3.1 8B Instruct use per million output tokens?

Llama 3.1 8B Instruct uses 13.0 Wh of GPU energy per million output tokens on 1 × B200 and 19.5 Wh of GPU energy per million output tokens on 1 × H100 at the most energy-efficient configuration measured (ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0, Text Conversation, data compiled 16 February 2026). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted, so it is a floor.

### Is Llama 3.1 8B Instruct more energy-efficient on B200 or H100?

On the index rows, the H100 configuration uses 1.50× the energy per token of the B200 configuration: 19.5 Wh/M on 1 × H100 against 13.0 Wh/M on 1 × B200. Both are floors at high load.

### How much does load change the energy per token of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct?

On 1 × H100, energy per token falls 6.5× between a running batch of 8 (126.3 Wh/M) and 511 (19.5 Wh/M), because the cards' power rises only 41 percent while throughput rises 9.2×. A server holding a handful of requests at a time sits at the top of that range.

### What is the carbon footprint of a billion tokens of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct?

A billion output tokens of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct on 1 × B200 at its index row carries about 8.9 kg CO2e of GPU-side emissions on the Saudi grid (689 gCO2e per kWh, Ember 2024) and 0.4 kg on the Norwegian grid (30). Multiply the Wh/M figure by your own grid's intensity and divide by 1,000 for kilograms per billion tokens.

### Is this the energy my Llama 3.1 8B Instruct deployment will use?

No. Every figure here is the lowest-energy configuration under the leaderboard's 500 ms median inter-token latency ceiling, on a busy server, GPU only. Your deployment sits above it, often several times above it; the configuration table shows how far. To get your own figure, follow the measurement protocol on the contribute page.

### Where do these figures come from?

The ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (The ML.ENERGY Initiative), released 1 December 2025, data compiled 16 February 2026, retrieved 26 September 2026: 20 stable configurations of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct measured with Zeus under vLLM on H100 80GB and B200 servers. Grid intensities are Ember's 2024 yearly figures. Lead Green recomputes every number from dated snapshots.

*Sources*

## Where every figure came from

[ML.ENERGY Leaderboard](https://ml.energy/leaderboard/) version 3.0 (released 1 December 2025; data compiled 16 February 2026; retrieved 26 September 2026), The ML.ENERGY Initiative, started at SymbioticLab, University of Michigan. Text Conversation task, 328 stable configurations. Energy per token is steady-state GPU energy divided by the output tokens generated in the window, measured with Zeus under vLLM 0.11.1 on H100 80GB HBM3 and B200 servers; energy per request is that figure times the average output length. Each index row is the lowest-energy configuration for its model and GPU at or under a 500 ms median inter-token latency, the leaderboard's own default ceiling, which no configuration reaches. Apache 2.0 per the [ml-energy/benchmark-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ml-energy/benchmark-v3) dataset card. Cite [Chung et al., The ML.ENERGY Benchmark, NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06371).

Grid intensity: [Ember, Yearly electricity data](https://ember-energy.org/data/yearly-electricity-data/), October 2026 release, 2024 (CC BY 4.0). Model card: [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct).

**Cite as.** Lead Green, a Katonic project. Green Tokens: GPU energy per million output tokens. https://leadgreen.ai/index/, release 2026-10-19, retrieved [date]. © 2026 Katonic AI Technology Ltd. Licensed [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), offered as-is and without warranty; state whether you changed any rows or columns. Underlying data: ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (The ML.ENERGY Initiative; Apache 2.0 per the ml-energy/benchmark-v3 dataset card; cite Chung et al., The ML.ENERGY Benchmark, NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks, arXiv 2505.06371); Ember, Yearly electricity data, October 2026 release (CC BY 4.0); AI Energy Score (Apache-2.0 as tagged on its Space; results reproduced as facts with attribution); NVIDIA figures reproduced as facts from the documents named in the sources ledger.

This page is generated from the same dated snapshot as [the index](https://leadgreen.ai/index/) and [the API](https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/models/llama-3-1-8b-instruct.json); no figure on it is typed by hand. Ask the [MCP server](https://leadgreen.ai/mcp/) for Llama 3.1 8B Instruct on your own grid and load.

*Two tasks*

## Long answers cost more per token too

On the leaderboard's Problem Solving task, Qwen 3 8B costs 38.3× the energy per response and 3.06× the energy per token on 1 × H100 (answers of 8,052 tokens against 645; running batch 82 against 474) and 40.6× the energy per response and 3.26× the energy per token on 1 × B200 (answers of 8,074 tokens against 649; running batch 128 against 1,427), compared with Text Conversation. The long answers cut the batch the server can hold, which is why energy per token itself moves. All 11 pairs are on [the index](https://leadgreen.ai/index/#workloads).

Every figure is a floor; a lightly used server sits well above it. Machine-readable data: https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/ (see llms.txt).

*[Models](https://leadgreen.ai/models/) · B200 and H100*

Qwen 3 14B serves a million output tokens for **15.2 Wh/M** on 1 × B200 (running batch 2,045, median inter-token latency 113 ms) and **31.1 Wh/M** on 1 × H100 (running batch 253, median inter-token latency 38 ms), GPU energy only, at the most energy-efficient configuration the ML.ENERGY Leaderboard measured. That is the floor: a lightly loaded server sits above it.

*Every configuration*

## Qwen 3 14B at every measured load

On 1 × B200, Qwen 3 14B runs from **194.3 Wh/M** at a running batch of 8 to **15.2 Wh/M** at 2,045, a fall of 12.8×, while the cards' draw rises 14 percent (from 760 to 869 W) and throughput rises 14.6× (from 1,087 to 15,875 tokens a second). Median inter-token latency stays at 113 ms or under up to the best row.

*Two generations*

## H100 against B200

On the index rows, the H100 configuration uses 2.04× the energy per token of the B200 configuration: 31.1 Wh/M on 1 × H100 against 15.2 Wh/M on 1 × B200. The two rows were not swept alike: the H100 row holds a running batch of 253 on 1 card and the B200 row 2,045 on 1, so part of the gap is the sweep, not the silicon. The full comparison across 14 models is on [the index](https://leadgreen.ai/index/#generations).

*Carbon*

## Same tokens, different grid

A billion output tokens of Qwen 3 14B on 1 × B200 at its index row carries about 10.5 kg CO2e of GPU-side emissions on the Saudi grid (689 gCO2e per kWh, Ember 2024) and 0.5 kg on the Norwegian grid (30). Energy per token does not change with geography; carbon per token does.

|---|---|---|

| Hong Kong | 676 | 10.3 |
| Serbia | 668 | 10.2 |
| World | 473 | 7.2 |
| Germany | 340 | 5.2 |
| Norway | 30 | 0.5 |

Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000. Lifecycle emissions intensity: CO2e per kWh of net generation, built from per-technology lifecycle factors (IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III midpoints, all gases at GWP-100), so upstream methane, supply chains and plant manufacture are included. Production-based: imports and grid losses are excluded. A location-based figure for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported. All 193 grids are in [grid.json](https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/grid.json); the [MCP server](https://leadgreen.ai/mcp/) prices any model on any grid.

*Two tasks*

## Long answers cost more per token too

On the leaderboard's Problem Solving task, Qwen 3 14B costs 26.8× the energy per response and 2.50× the energy per token on 1 × H100 (answers of 6,711 tokens against 625; running batch 59 against 253) and 39.8× the energy per response and 3.33× the energy per token on 1 × B200 (answers of 7,327 tokens against 613; running batch 128 against 2,045), compared with Text Conversation. The long answers cut the batch the server can hold, which is why energy per token itself moves. All 11 pairs are on [the index](https://leadgreen.ai/index/#workloads).

*Questions*

## Asked about Qwen 3 14B

### How much energy does Qwen 3 14B use per million output tokens?

Qwen 3 14B uses 15.2 Wh of GPU energy per million output tokens on 1 × B200 and 31.1 Wh of GPU energy per million output tokens on 1 × H100 at the most energy-efficient configuration measured (ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0, Text Conversation, data compiled 16 February 2026). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted, so it is a floor.

### Is Qwen 3 14B more energy-efficient on B200 or H100?

On the index rows, the H100 configuration uses 2.04× the energy per token of the B200 configuration: 31.1 Wh/M on 1 × H100 against 15.2 Wh/M on 1 × B200. Both are floors at high load.

### How much does load change the energy per token of Qwen 3 14B?

On 1 × B200, energy per token falls 12.8× between a running batch of 8 (194.3 Wh/M) and 2,045 (15.2 Wh/M), because the cards' power rises only 14 percent while throughput rises 14.6×. A server holding a handful of requests at a time sits at the top of that range.

### What is the carbon footprint of a billion tokens of Qwen 3 14B?

A billion output tokens of Qwen 3 14B on 1 × B200 at its index row carries about 10.5 kg CO2e of GPU-side emissions on the Saudi grid (689 gCO2e per kWh, Ember 2024) and 0.5 kg on the Norwegian grid (30). Multiply the Wh/M figure by your own grid's intensity and divide by 1,000 for kilograms per billion tokens.

### Does Qwen 3 14B use more energy for reasoning or problem-solving tasks?

On the leaderboard's Problem Solving task, Qwen 3 14B costs 26.8× the energy per response and 2.50× the energy per token on 1 × H100 (answers of 6,711 tokens against 625; running batch 59 against 253) and 39.8× the energy per response and 3.33× the energy per token on 1 × B200 (answers of 7,327 tokens against 613; running batch 128 against 2,045), compared with Text Conversation.

### Is this the energy my Qwen 3 14B deployment will use?

No. Every figure here is the lowest-energy configuration under the leaderboard's 500 ms median inter-token latency ceiling, on a busy server, GPU only. Your deployment sits above it, often several times above it; the configuration table shows how far. To get your own figure, follow the measurement protocol on the contribute page.

### Where do these figures come from?

The ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (The ML.ENERGY Initiative), released 1 December 2025, data compiled 16 February 2026, retrieved 26 September 2026: 17 stable configurations of Qwen 3 14B measured with Zeus under vLLM on H100 80GB and B200 servers. Grid intensities are Ember's 2024 yearly figures. Lead Green recomputes every number from dated snapshots.

*Sources*

## Where every figure came from

[ML.ENERGY Leaderboard](https://ml.energy/leaderboard/) version 3.0 (released 1 December 2025; data compiled 16 February 2026; retrieved 26 September 2026), The ML.ENERGY Initiative, started at SymbioticLab, University of Michigan. Text Conversation task, 328 stable configurations. Energy per token is steady-state GPU energy divided by the output tokens generated in the window, measured with Zeus under vLLM 0.11.1 on H100 80GB HBM3 and B200 servers; energy per request is that figure times the average output length. Each index row is the lowest-energy configuration for its model and GPU at or under a 500 ms median inter-token latency, the leaderboard's own default ceiling, which no configuration reaches. Apache 2.0 per the [ml-energy/benchmark-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ml-energy/benchmark-v3) dataset card. *Every configuration*

## Gemma 3 12B at every measured load

On 1 × B200, Gemma 3 12B runs from **185.9 Wh/M** at a running batch of 8 to **26.5 Wh/M** at 487, a fall of 7.0×, while the cards' draw rises 39 percent (from 668 to 928 W) and throughput rises 9.8× (from 998 to 9,733 tokens a second). Median inter-token latency stays at 44 ms or under up to the best row.

| 16 | 16 | 109.5 | 8 | 1,726 | 681 |
| 32 | 32 | 68.5 | 11 | 2,535 | 625 |

Cap is the configured maximum batch (vLLM's `max_num_seqs`). The highlighted row is the index row for that GPU. Wh/M is derived from the source's joules per output token; prompt processing is included.

*Two generations*

## H100 against B200

On the index rows, the H100 configuration uses 1.74× the energy per token of the B200 configuration: 46.1 Wh/M on 1 × H100 against 26.5 Wh/M on 1 × B200. The two rows were not swept alike: the H100 row holds a running batch of 128 on 1 card and the B200 row 487 on 1, so part of the gap is the sweep, not the silicon. The full comparison across 14 models is on [the index](https://leadgreen.ai/index/#generations).

*Carbon*

## Same tokens, different grid

A billion output tokens of Gemma 3 12B on 1 × B200 at its index row carries about 18.3 kg CO2e of GPU-side emissions on the Saudi grid (689 gCO2e per kWh, Ember 2024) and 0.8 kg on the Norwegian grid (30). Energy per token does not change with geography; carbon per token does.

| Serbia | 668 | 17.7 |
| World | 473 | 12.5 |
| Germany | 340 | 9.0 |
| Norway | 30 | 0.8 |

Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000. Lifecycle emissions intensity: CO2e per kWh of net generation, built from per-technology lifecycle factors (IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III midpoints, all gases at GWP-100), so upstream methane, supply chains and plant manufacture are included. Production-based: imports and grid losses are excluded. A location-based figure for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported. *Questions*

## Asked about Gemma 3 12B

### How much energy does Gemma 3 12B use per million output tokens?

Gemma 3 12B uses 26.5 Wh of GPU energy per million output tokens on 1 × B200 and 46.1 Wh of GPU energy per million output tokens on 1 × H100 at the most energy-efficient configuration measured (ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0, Text Conversation, data compiled 16 February 2026). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted, so it is a floor.

### Is Gemma 3 12B more energy-efficient on B200 or H100?

On the index rows, the H100 configuration uses 1.74× the energy per token of the B200 configuration: 46.1 Wh/M on 1 × H100 against 26.5 Wh/M on 1 × B200. Both are floors at high load.

### How much does load change the energy per token of Gemma 3 12B?

On 1 × B200, energy per token falls 7.0× between a running batch of 8 (185.9 Wh/M) and 487 (26.5 Wh/M), because the cards' power rises only 39 percent while throughput rises 9.8×. A server holding a handful of requests at a time sits at the top of that range.

### What is the carbon footprint of a billion tokens of Gemma 3 12B?

A billion output tokens of Gemma 3 12B on 1 × B200 at its index row carries about 18.3 kg CO2e of GPU-side emissions on the Saudi grid (689 gCO2e per kWh, Ember 2024) and 0.8 kg on the Norwegian grid (30). Multiply the Wh/M figure by your own grid's intensity and divide by 1,000 for kilograms per billion tokens.

### Is this the energy my Gemma 3 12B deployment will use?

No. Every figure here is the lowest-energy configuration under the leaderboard's 500 ms median inter-token latency ceiling, on a busy server, GPU only. Your deployment sits above it, often several times above it; the configuration table shows how far. To get your own figure, follow the measurement protocol on the contribute page.

### Where do these figures come from?

The ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (The ML.ENERGY Initiative), released 1 December 2025, data compiled 16 February 2026, retrieved 26 September 2026: 13 stable configurations of Gemma 3 12B measured with Zeus under vLLM on H100 80GB and B200 servers. Grid intensities are Ember's 2024 yearly figures. Lead Green recomputes every number from dated snapshots.

*Sources*

## Where every figure came from

[ML.ENERGY Leaderboard](https://ml.energy/leaderboard/) version 3.0 (released 1 December 2025; data compiled 16 February 2026; retrieved 26 September 2026), The ML.ENERGY Initiative, started at SymbioticLab, University of Michigan. Text Conversation task, 328 stable configurations. Energy per token is steady-state GPU energy divided by the output tokens generated in the window, measured with Zeus under vLLM 0.11.1 on H100 80GB HBM3 and B200 servers; energy per request is that figure times the average output length. Each index row is the lowest-energy configuration for its model and GPU at or under a 500 ms median inter-token latency, the leaderboard's own default ceiling, which no configuration reaches. Apache 2.0 per the [ml-energy/benchmark-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ml-energy/benchmark-v3) dataset card. Cite [Chung et al., The ML.ENERGY Benchmark, NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06371).

Grid intensity: [Ember, Yearly electricity data](https://ember-energy.org/data/yearly-electricity-data/), October 2026 release, 2024 (CC BY 4.0). Model card: [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-3-12b-it).

## Qwen 3 32B at every measured load

On 1 × B200, Qwen 3 32B runs from **429.2 Wh/M** at a running batch of 8 to **39.1 Wh/M** at 383, a fall of 11.0×, while the cards' draw rises 13 percent (from 860 to 972 W) and throughput rises 12.4× (from 556 to 6,912 tokens a second). Median inter-token latency stays at 50 ms or under up to the best row. Past it, at a cap of 512, the same cards read 41.9 Wh/M at 58 ms.

*Two tasks*

## Long answers cost more per token too

On the leaderboard's Problem Solving task, Qwen 3 32B costs 24.6× the energy per response and 2.22× the energy per token on 1 × B200 (answers of 7,035 tokens against 635; running batch 111 against 383) and 26.1× the energy per response and 2.35× the energy per token on 2 × H100 (answers of 7,058 tokens against 634; running batch 64 against 256), compared with Text Conversation. The long answers cut the batch the server can hold, which is why energy per token itself moves. All 11 pairs are on [the index](https://leadgreen.ai/index/#workloads).

On the leaderboard's Problem Solving task, NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 12B V2 costs 3.9× the energy per response and 1.02× the energy per token on 1 × B200 (answers of 5,646 tokens against 1,464; running batch 256 against 256) and 8.7× the energy per response and 0.70× the energy per token on 1 × H100 (answers of 5,768 tokens against 462; running batch 192 against 241), compared with Text Conversation. The long answers cut the batch the server can hold, which is why energy per token itself moves. All 11 pairs are on [the index](https://leadgreen.ai/index/#workloads).

*Questions*

## Asked about NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 12B V2

### How much energy does NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 12B V2 use per million output tokens?

NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 12B V2 uses 39.4 Wh of GPU energy per million output tokens on 1 × B200 and 50.1 Wh of GPU energy per million output tokens on 1 × H100 at the most energy-efficient configuration measured (ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0, Text Conversation, data compiled 16 February 2026). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted, so it is a floor.

### Is NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 12B V2 more energy-efficient on B200 or H100?

On the index rows, the H100 configuration uses 1.27× the energy per token of the B200 configuration: 50.1 Wh/M on 1 × H100 against 39.4 Wh/M on 1 × B200. Both are floors at high load.

### How much does load change the energy per token of NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 12B V2?

On 1 × H100, energy per token falls 4.1× between a running batch of 8 (207.6 Wh/M) and 241 (50.1 Wh/M), because the cards' power rises only 39 percent while throughput rises 5.8×. A server holding a handful of requests at a time sits at the top of that range.

### What is the carbon footprint of a billion tokens of NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 12B V2?

A billion output tokens of NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 12B V2 on 1 × B200 at its index row carries about 27.2 kg CO2e of GPU-side emissions on the Saudi grid (689 gCO2e per kWh, Ember 2024) and 1.2 kg on the Norwegian grid (30). Multiply the Wh/M figure by your own grid's intensity and divide by 1,000 for kilograms per billion tokens.

### Does NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 12B V2 use more energy for reasoning or problem-solving tasks?

On the leaderboard's Problem Solving task, NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 12B V2 costs 3.9× the energy per response and 1.02× the energy per token on 1 × B200 (answers of 5,646 tokens against 1,464; running batch 256 against 256) and 8.7× the energy per response and 0.70× the energy per token on 1 × H100 (answers of 5,768 tokens against 462; running batch 192 against 241), compared with Text Conversation.

### Is this the energy my NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 12B V2 deployment will use?

No. Every figure here is the lowest-energy configuration under the leaderboard's 500 ms median inter-token latency ceiling, on a busy server, GPU only. Your deployment sits above it, often several times above it; the configuration table shows how far. To get your own figure, follow the measurement protocol on the contribute page.

### Where do these figures come from?

The ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (The ML.ENERGY Initiative), released 1 December 2025, data compiled 16 February 2026, retrieved 26 September 2026: 14 stable configurations of NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 12B V2 measured with Zeus under vLLM on H100 80GB and B200 servers. Grid intensities are Ember's 2024 yearly figures. Lead Green recomputes every number from dated snapshots.

*Sources*

## Where every figure came from

[ML.ENERGY Leaderboard](https://ml.energy/leaderboard/) version 3.0 (released 1 December 2025; data compiled 16 February 2026; retrieved 26 September 2026), The ML.ENERGY Initiative, started at SymbioticLab, University of Michigan. Text Conversation task, 328 stable configurations. Energy per token is steady-state GPU energy divided by the output tokens generated in the window, measured with Zeus under vLLM 0.11.1 on H100 80GB HBM3 and B200 servers; energy per request is that figure times the average output length. Each index row is the lowest-energy configuration for its model and GPU at or under a 500 ms median inter-token latency, the leaderboard's own default ceiling, which no configuration reaches. ## NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 9B V2 at every measured load

On 1 × H100, NVIDIA Nemotron Nano 9B V2 runs from **162.7 Wh/M** at a running batch of 8 to **43.1 Wh/M** at 255, a fall of 3.8×, while the cards' draw rises 48 percent (from 467 to 693 W) and throughput rises 5.6× (from 797 to 4,465 tokens a second). Median inter-token latency stays at 43 ms or under up to the best row.

*Questions*

## Asked about Gemma 3 27B

### How much energy does Gemma 3 27B use per million output tokens?

Gemma 3 27B uses 49.1 Wh of GPU energy per million output tokens on 1 × B200 and 80.4 Wh of GPU energy per million output tokens on 2 × H100 at the most energy-efficient configuration measured (ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0, Text Conversation, data compiled 16 February 2026). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted, so it is a floor.

### Is Gemma 3 27B more energy-efficient on B200 or H100?

On the index rows, the H100 configuration uses 1.64× the energy per token of the B200 configuration: 80.4 Wh/M on 2 × H100 against 49.1 Wh/M on 1 × B200. Both are floors at high load.

### How much does load change the energy per token of Gemma 3 27B?

On 2 × H100, energy per token falls 5.3× between a running batch of 8 (430.2 Wh/M) and 187 (80.4 Wh/M), because the cards' power rises only 49 percent while throughput rises 8.0×. A server holding a handful of requests at a time sits at the top of that range.

### What is the carbon footprint of a billion tokens of Gemma 3 27B?

A billion output tokens of Gemma 3 27B on 1 × B200 at its index row carries about 33.8 kg CO2e of GPU-side emissions on the Saudi grid (689 gCO2e per kWh, Ember 2024) and 1.5 kg on the Norwegian grid (30). Multiply the Wh/M figure by your own grid's intensity and divide by 1,000 for kilograms per billion tokens.

### Is this the energy my Gemma 3 27B deployment will use?

No. Every figure here is the lowest-energy configuration under the leaderboard's 500 ms median inter-token latency ceiling, on a busy server, GPU only. Your deployment sits above it, often several times above it; the configuration table shows how far. To get your own figure, follow the measurement protocol on the contribute page.

### Where do these figures come from?

The ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (The ML.ENERGY Initiative), released 1 December 2025, data compiled 16 February 2026, retrieved 26 September 2026: 16 stable configurations of Gemma 3 27B measured with Zeus under vLLM on H100 80GB and B200 servers. Grid intensities are Ember's 2024 yearly figures. Lead Green recomputes every number from dated snapshots.

*Two generations*

## H100 against B200

On the index rows, the H100 configuration uses 4.55× the energy per token of the B200 configuration: 303.5 Wh/M on 8 × H100 against 66.7 Wh/M on 4 × B200. The two rows were not swept alike: the H100 row holds a running batch of 228 on 8 cards and the B200 row 3,765 on 4, so part of the gap is the sweep, not the silicon. The full comparison across 14 models is on [the index](https://leadgreen.ai/index/#generations).

*Carbon*

## Same tokens, different grid

A billion output tokens of Qwen 3 235B A22B Instruct on 4 × B200 at its index row carries about 46.0 kg CO2e of GPU-side emissions on the Saudi grid (689 gCO2e per kWh, Ember 2024) and 2.0 kg on the Norwegian grid (30). Energy per token does not change with geography; carbon per token does.

Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000. Lifecycle emissions intensity: CO2e per kWh of net generation, built from per-technology lifecycle factors (IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III midpoints, all gases at GWP-100), so upstream methane, supply chains and plant manufacture are included. Production-based: imports and grid losses are excluded. A location-based figure for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported. ### Is Qwen 3 235B A22B Instruct more energy-efficient on B200 or H100?

On the index rows, the H100 configuration uses 4.55× the energy per token of the B200 configuration: 303.5 Wh/M on 8 × H100 against 66.7 Wh/M on 4 × B200. Both are floors at high load.

### How much does load change the energy per token of Qwen 3 235B A22B Instruct?

On 4 × B200, energy per token falls 26.9× between a running batch of 8 (1,793.5 Wh/M) and 3,765 (66.7 Wh/M), because the cards' power rises only 25 percent while throughput rises 33.5×. A server holding a handful of requests at a time sits at the top of that range.

### What is the carbon footprint of a billion tokens of Qwen 3 235B A22B Instruct?

A billion output tokens of Qwen 3 235B A22B Instruct on 4 × B200 at its index row carries about 46.0 kg CO2e of GPU-side emissions on the Saudi grid (689 gCO2e per kWh, Ember 2024) and 2.0 kg on the Norwegian grid (30). *Every configuration*

## Llama 4 Maverick 17B 128E Instruct FP8 at every measured load

On 8 × H100, Llama 4 Maverick 17B 128E Instruct FP8 runs from **779.0 Wh/M** at a running batch of 8 to **134.5 Wh/M** at 383, a fall of 5.8×, while the cards' draw rises 88 percent (from 1,845 to 3,462 W) and throughput rises 10.9× (from 658 to 7,149 tokens a second). Median inter-token latency stays at 48 ms or under up to the best row.

*Llama 4 Maverick 17B 128E Instruct FP8, FP8, 8 × H100: nine measured configurations*

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 8 | 779.0 | 11 | 658 | 1,845 |
| 16 | 16 | 504.4 | 13 | 1,110 | 2,015 |
| 32 | 32 | 351.5 | 16 | 1,805 | 2,284 |
| 64 | 64 | 262.2 | 21 | 2,813 | 2,656 |
| 96 | 96 | 235.8 | 25 | 3,546 | 3,010 |
| 128 | 128 | 210.4 | 28 | 4,147 | 3,141 |
| 192 | 192 | 178.2 | 33 | 5,210 | 3,343 |
| 256 | 255 | 155.7 | 37 | 6,258 | 3,507 |
| 384 | 383 | 134.5 | 48 | 7,149 | 3,462 |

Cap is the configured maximum batch (vLLM's `max_num_seqs`). Running batch (avg) is the average number of requests the server was decoding at once over the steady-state window (vLLM's `num_requests_running`); queued requests are not counted. The highlighted row is the index row for that GPU. Wh/M is derived from the source's joules per output token; prompt processing is included.

## Asked about Llama 4 Maverick 17B 128E Instruct FP8

### How much energy does Llama 4 Maverick 17B 128E Instruct FP8 use per million output tokens?

Llama 4 Maverick 17B 128E Instruct FP8 uses 134.5 Wh of GPU energy per million output tokens on 8 × H100 at the most energy-efficient configuration measured (ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0, Text Conversation, data compiled 16 February 2026). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted, so it is a floor.

### How much does load change the energy per token of Llama 4 Maverick 17B 128E Instruct FP8?

On 8 × H100, energy per token falls 5.8× between a running batch of 8 (779.0 Wh/M) and 383 (134.5 Wh/M), because the cards' power rises only 88 percent while throughput rises 10.9×. A server holding a handful of requests at a time sits at the top of that range.

### What is the carbon footprint of a billion tokens of Llama 4 Maverick 17B 128E Instruct FP8?

A billion output tokens of Llama 4 Maverick 17B 128E Instruct FP8 on 8 × H100 at its index row carries about 92.7 kg CO2e of GPU-side emissions on the Saudi grid (689 gCO2e per kWh, Ember 2024) and 4.0 kg on the Norwegian grid (30). Multiply the Wh/M figure by your own grid's intensity and divide by 1,000 for kilograms per billion tokens.

### Is this the energy my Llama 4 Maverick 17B 128E Instruct FP8 deployment will use?

No. Every figure here is the lowest-energy configuration under the leaderboard's 500 ms median inter-token latency ceiling, on a busy server, GPU only. Your deployment sits above it, often several times above it; the configuration table shows how far. To get your own figure, follow the measurement protocol on the contribute page.

### Where do these figures come from?

The ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (The ML.ENERGY Initiative), released 1 December 2025, data compiled 16 February 2026, retrieved 26 September 2026: 9 stable configurations of Llama 4 Maverick 17B 128E Instruct FP8 measured with Zeus under vLLM on H100 80GB and B200 servers. Grid intensities are Ember's 2024 yearly figures. Lead Green recomputes every number from dated snapshots.

## Where every figure came from

[ML.ENERGY Leaderboard](https://ml.energy/leaderboard/) version 3.0 (released 1 December 2025; data compiled 16 February 2026; retrieved 26 September 2026), The ML.ENERGY Initiative, started at SymbioticLab, University of Michigan. Text Conversation task, 328 stable configurations. Energy per token is steady-state GPU energy divided by the output tokens generated in the window, measured with Zeus under vLLM 0.11.1 on H100 80GB HBM3 and B200 servers; energy per request is that figure times the average output length. Each index row is the lowest-energy configuration for its model and GPU at or under a 500 ms median inter-token latency, the leaderboard's own default ceiling, which no configuration reaches. Apache 2.0 per the [ml-energy/benchmark-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ml-energy/benchmark-v3) dataset card. Cite [Chung et al., The ML.ENERGY Benchmark, NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06371).

Grid intensity: [Ember, Yearly electricity data](https://ember-energy.org/data/yearly-electricity-data/), October 2026 release, 2024 (CC BY 4.0). Model card: [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8).

The highlighted row is the index row for that GPU. Wh/M is derived from the source's joules per output token; prompt processing is included.

*Two tasks*

## Long answers cost more per token too

On the leaderboard's Problem Solving task, DeepSeek V3.1 costs 23.5× the energy per response and 2.20× the energy per token on 8 × B200 (answers of 8,969 tokens against 842; running batch 256 against 3,008), compared with Text Conversation. The long answers cut the batch the server can hold, which is why energy per token itself moves. All 11 pairs are on [the index](https://leadgreen.ai/index/#workloads).

*Questions*

## Asked about DeepSeek V3.1

### How much energy does DeepSeek V3.1 use per million output tokens?

DeepSeek V3.1 uses 168.4 Wh of GPU energy per million output tokens on 8 × B200 at the most energy-efficient configuration measured (ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0, Text Conversation, data compiled 16 February 2026). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted, so it is a floor.

### How much does load change the energy per token of DeepSeek V3.1?

On 8 × B200, energy per token falls 14.1× between a running batch of 8 (2,379.3 Wh/M) and 3,008 (168.4 Wh/M), because the cards' power rises only 42 percent while throughput rises 20.1×. A server holding a handful of requests at a time sits at the top of that range.

### What is the carbon footprint of a billion tokens of DeepSeek V3.1?

A billion output tokens of DeepSeek V3.1 on 8 × B200 at its index row carries about 116.1 kg CO2e of GPU-side emissions on the Saudi grid (689 gCO2e per kWh, Ember 2024) and 5.0 kg on the Norwegian grid (30). Multiply the Wh/M figure by your own grid's intensity and divide by 1,000 for kilograms per billion tokens.

### Does DeepSeek V3.1 use more energy for reasoning or problem-solving tasks?

On the leaderboard's Problem Solving task, DeepSeek V3.1 costs 23.5× the energy per response and 2.20× the energy per token on 8 × B200 (answers of 8,969 tokens against 842; running batch 256 against 3,008), compared with Text Conversation.

### Is this the energy my DeepSeek V3.1 deployment will use?

No. Every figure here is the lowest-energy configuration under the leaderboard's 500 ms median inter-token latency ceiling, on a busy server, GPU only. Your deployment sits above it, often several times above it; the configuration table shows how far. To get your own figure, follow the measurement protocol on the contribute page.

### Where do these figures come from?

The ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (The ML.ENERGY Initiative), released 1 December 2025, data compiled 16 February 2026, retrieved 26 September 2026: 11 stable configurations of DeepSeek V3.1 measured with Zeus under vLLM on H100 80GB and B200 servers. Grid intensities are Ember's 2024 yearly figures. Lead Green recomputes every number from dated snapshots.

*Sources*

Energy per token is steady-state GPU energy divided by the output tokens generated in the window, measured with Zeus under vLLM 0.11.1 on H100 80GB HBM3 and B200 servers; energy per request is that figure times the average output length. # India: the carbon of AI inference per billion tokens

> About 44.9 kg CO2e per billion LLM output tokens (44.9 g per million) on India's grid (707 gCO2e/kWh, 2024, Ember), every index model priced.
>
> Lead Green, a Katonic project. Canonical page: https://leadgreen.ai/grids/india/ (this file: https://leadgreen.ai/grids/india/index.md). Updated 19 October 2026, data version 2026-10-19. Licence: CC BY 4.0 for the compilation and text; sources keep their own licences. GPU energy only, measured at steady state on a busy server (the most energy-efficient configuration under a latency limit). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted. Every figure is a floor; a lightly used server sits well above it. Machine-readable data: https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/ (see llms.txt).

*[Grids](https://leadgreen.ai/grids/) · Asia · a market Katonic sells in or expects to*

An LLM served on India's grid emits about **44.9 kg CO2e per billion output tokens**, 44.9 g per million, at the index's reference row (Qwen 3 32B, 2 × H100, 63.5 Wh/M), GPU energy only; the index's lowest row emits 9.2 kg and its highest 405.1 kg. The grid ran at **707 gCO2e per kWh** in 2024 on Ember's yearly figures, 1.5× the world average of 473, and 181st of the 193 countries Ember covers, counting from the cleanest. Energy per token does not change with geography; carbon per token does.

**Area** India (IND, IN). **Basis** lifecycle, location-based, annual average. **Data** [grid.json](https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/grid.json). Updated 19 October 2026.

Cite this page: Lead Green, a Katonic project. India: carbon of AI inference per billion tokens. https://leadgreen.ai/grids/india/, release 2026-10-19, retrieved [date]. CC BY 4.0.

- [Trend](https://leadgreen.ai/grids/india/#trend)
- [Every model](https://leadgreen.ai/grids/india/#models)

- [Questions](https://leadgreen.ai/grids/india/#faq)
- [Sources](https://leadgreen.ai/grids/india/#sources)

- **Grid intensity, 2024:** 707 gCO2e/kWh Ember yearly data, lifecycle, location-based. World: 473.
- **Reference row, per billion tokens:** 44.9 kg CO2e Qwen 3 32B, 2 × H100, 63.5 Wh/M, GPU only, a floor.
- **Rank:** 181 of 193 1 is the cleanest grid Ember covers (Ethiopia, 23); 193 the highest (Turkmenistan, 1,306).

Carbon per token is energy per token times the grid. The energy figures here are GPU-only floors from a busy server; a lightly loaded deployment sits above them, and so does anything that includes the host, the network and the cooling. Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000 gives kg CO2e per billion output tokens.

*Trend*

## India's grid, year by year

From 2023 to 2025 the intensity fell 6 percent, from 714.2 to 670.9 gCO2e per kWh. The table uses 2024, the latest year with a value for every listed grid; on the 2025 figure the reference row would carry 42.6 kg per billion tokens.

*Ember yearly emissions intensity for India, and the reference row priced on each year*

| Year | g CO2e per kWh | kg CO2e per billion tokens, reference row |
|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 714.2 | 45.3 |
| 2024 | 707.1 | 44.9 |
| 2025 | 670.9 | 42.6 |

Lifecycle emissions intensity: CO2e per kWh of net generation, built from per-technology lifecycle factors (IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III midpoints, all gases at GWP-100), so upstream methane, supply chains and plant manufacture are included. Production-based: imports and grid losses are excluded. A location-based figure for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported. A GPU server draws much the same power around the clock, while an annual average weights each hour by its generation, so on a grid whose clean supply peaks at midday a flat load sees a higher figure than the average.

*Every model*

Each model's lowest index row, GPU only, at the most energy-efficient configuration measured, multiplied by 707 gCO2e per kWh. The spread from the lowest row to the highest is 44×, and it is entirely the model, the GPU and the load; the grid multiplies all of them alike.

*Reporting*

## Which line it goes on

For GPUs you run in India, the electricity is your own consumption: it goes into your ESRS E1-5 energy total and its emissions into E1-6 as Scope 2, location-based, which is the method this page's figure matches. The market-based figure nets your contracted supply and needs your own contracts. Tokens bought from a hosted API are the provider's Scope 2 and your Scope 3 category 1, and sit outside your E1-5 line; [the why page](https://leadgreen.ai/why/#hosted) lists what to ask the provider. Ember's figure is a lifecycle intensity for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported.

*Questions*

## Asked about AI carbon in India

### What is the grid carbon intensity of India?

707 gCO2e per kWh in 2024, on Ember's yearly electricity data: a lifecycle, location-based figure for the country's own generation, 1.5× the world average of 473. Ember's 2025 figure is 670.9.

### How much CO2 does a million AI tokens produce in India?

At the index's reference row (Qwen 3 32B on 2 × H100, 63.5 Wh per million output tokens, GPU only), about 44.9 grams of CO2e per million tokens, or 44.9 kg per billion, on India's 2024 grid. Across the index the range is 9.2 to 405.1 kg per billion tokens. A lightly loaded server sits above these floors, and host, network and cooling are not counted.

### Is running AI in India cleaner than the world average?

India's 2024 intensity of 707 gCO2e per kWh is 1.5× the world average of 473 (473 gCO2e per kWh). The same tokens on the same GPUs produce the same energy figure anywhere; only the carbon figure moves with the grid.

### Can I use this figure for my Scope 2 report in India?

As a comparison, not as a filing. Ember's intensity is a lifecycle figure on net generation, not a Scope 2 combustion factor, and it is location-based; a market-based figure needs your own contracted supply. Tokens bought from a hosted API land in your Scope 3 category 1, not your Scope 2. The why page explains both.

### Where do these figures come from?

Grid intensity: Ember, Yearly electricity data, October 2026 release (2024; 2023, 2024, 2025 shown), CC BY 4.0, retrieved 17 October 2026. Energy per token: the ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (data compiled 16 February 2026). Carbon is Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000.

*Sources*

## Where every figure came from

Grid intensity: [Ember, Yearly electricity data](https://ember-energy.org/data/yearly-electricity-data/), October 2026 release, emissions intensity of total generation, 2023, 2024, 2025 (CC BY 4.0), retrieved 17 October 2026. Energy per token: [ML.ENERGY Leaderboard](https://ml.energy/leaderboard/) version 3.0 (released 1 December 2025; data compiled 16 February 2026; retrieved 26 September 2026), The ML.ENERGY Initiative, started at SymbioticLab, University of Michigan. Text Conversation task, 328 stable configurations. Energy per token is steady-state GPU energy divided by the output tokens generated in the window, measured with Zeus under vLLM 0.11.1 on H100 80GB HBM3 and B200 servers; energy per request is that figure times the average output length. Each index row is the lowest-energy configuration for its model and GPU at or under a 500 ms median inter-token latency, the leaderboard's own default ceiling, which no configuration reaches. Apache 2.0 per the [ml-energy/benchmark-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ml-energy/benchmark-v3) dataset card. Cite [Chung et al., The ML.ENERGY Benchmark, NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06371).

## Asked about AI carbon in Saudi Arabia

### What is the grid carbon intensity of Saudi Arabia?

689 gCO2e per kWh in 2024, on Ember's yearly electricity data: a lifecycle, location-based figure for the country's own generation, 1.5× the world average of 473. Ember's 2025 figure is 679.8.

### How much CO2 does a million AI tokens produce in Saudi Arabia?

At the index's reference row (Qwen 3 32B on 2 × H100, 63.5 Wh per million output tokens, GPU only), about 43.7 grams of CO2e per million tokens, or 43.7 kg per billion, on Saudi Arabia's 2024 grid. Across the index the range is 8.9 to 394.8 kg per billion tokens. A lightly loaded server sits above these floors, and host, network and cooling are not counted.

### Is running AI in Saudi Arabia cleaner than the world average?

Saudi Arabia's 2024 intensity of 689 gCO2e per kWh is 1.5× the world average of 473 (473 gCO2e per kWh). The same tokens on the same GPUs produce the same energy figure anywhere; only the carbon figure moves with the grid.

### Can I use this figure for my Scope 2 report in Saudi Arabia?

As a comparison, not as a filing. Ember's intensity is a lifecycle figure on net generation, not a Scope 2 combustion factor, and it is location-based; a market-based figure needs your own contracted supply. Tokens bought from a hosted API land in your Scope 3 category 1, not your Scope 2. The why page explains both.

### Where do these figures come from?

Grid intensity: Ember, Yearly electricity data, October 2026 release (2024; 2023, 2024, 2025 shown), CC BY 4.0, retrieved 17 October 2026. Energy per token: the ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (data compiled 16 February 2026). Carbon is Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000.

*Sources*

## Where every figure came from

Grid intensity: [Ember, Yearly electricity data](https://ember-energy.org/data/yearly-electricity-data/), October 2026 release, emissions intensity of total generation, 2023, 2024, 2025 (CC BY 4.0), retrieved 17 October 2026. Energy per token: [ML.ENERGY Leaderboard](https://ml.energy/leaderboard/) version 3.0 (released 1 December 2025; data compiled 16 February 2026; retrieved 26 September 2026), The ML.ENERGY Initiative, started at SymbioticLab, University of Michigan. Text Conversation task, 328 stable configurations. Energy per token is steady-state GPU energy divided by the output tokens generated in the window, measured with Zeus under vLLM 0.11.1 on H100 80GB HBM3 and B200 servers; energy per request is that figure times the average output length. Each index row is the lowest-energy configuration for its model and GPU at or under a 500 ms median inter-token latency, the leaderboard's own default ceiling, which no configuration reaches. Apache 2.0 per the [ml-energy/benchmark-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ml-energy/benchmark-v3) dataset card. Cite [Chung et al., The ML.ENERGY Benchmark, NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06371).

Licensed [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), offered as-is and without warranty; state whether you changed any rows or columns. # Hong Kong: the carbon of AI inference per billion tokens

> About 42.9 kg CO2e per billion LLM output tokens (42.9 g per million) on Hong Kong's grid (676 gCO2e/kWh, 2024, Ember), every index model priced.

> Lead Green, a Katonic project. Canonical page: https://leadgreen.ai/grids/hong-kong/ (this file: https://leadgreen.ai/grids/hong-kong/index.md). Updated 19 October 2026, data version 2026-10-19. Licence: CC BY 4.0 for the compilation and text; sources keep their own licences. GPU energy only, measured at steady state on a busy server (the most energy-efficient configuration under a latency limit). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted. Every figure is a floor; a lightly used server sits well above it. Machine-readable data: https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/ (see llms.txt).

*[Grids](https://leadgreen.ai/grids/) · Asia · a market Katonic sells in or expects to*

An LLM served on Hong Kong's grid emits about **42.9 kg CO2e per billion output tokens**, 42.9 g per million, at the index's reference row (Qwen 3 32B, 2 × H100, 63.5 Wh/M), GPU energy only; the index's lowest row emits 8.8 kg and its highest 387.1 kg. The grid ran at **676 gCO2e per kWh** in 2024 on Ember's yearly figures, 1.4× the world average of 473, and 174th of the 193 countries Ember covers, counting from the cleanest. Energy per token does not change with geography; carbon per token does.

**Area** Hong Kong (SAR of China) (HKG, HK). **Basis** lifecycle, location-based, annual average. **Data** [grid.json](https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/grid.json). Updated 19 October 2026.

- **Grid intensity, 2024:** 676 gCO2e/kWh Ember yearly data, lifecycle, location-based. World: 473.
- **Reference row, per billion tokens:** 42.9 kg CO2e Qwen 3 32B, 2 × H100, 63.5 Wh/M, GPU only, a floor.
- **Rank:** 174 of 193 1 is the cleanest grid Ember covers (Ethiopia, 23); 193 the highest (Turkmenistan, 1,306).

Carbon per token is energy per token times the grid. The energy figures here are GPU-only floors from a busy server; a lightly loaded deployment sits above them, and so does anything that includes the host, the network and the cooling. Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000 gives kg CO2e per billion output tokens.

*Trend*

## Hong Kong's grid, year by year

From 2023 to 2024 the intensity was flat at about 675.6 gCO2e per kWh. 2024 is the latest year Ember publishes for Hong Kong.

*Ember yearly emissions intensity for Hong Kong, and the reference row priced on each year*

| Year | g CO2e per kWh | kg CO2e per billion tokens, reference row |
|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 674.3 | 42.8 |
| 2024 | 675.6 | 42.9 |

Lifecycle emissions intensity: CO2e per kWh of net generation, built from per-technology lifecycle factors (IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III midpoints, all gases at GWP-100), so upstream methane, supply chains and plant manufacture are included. Production-based: imports and grid losses are excluded. A location-based figure for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported. A GPU server draws much the same power around the clock, while an annual average weights each hour by its generation, so on a grid whose clean supply peaks at midday a flat load sees a higher figure than the average.

Each model's lowest index row, GPU only, at the most energy-efficient configuration measured, multiplied by 676 gCO2e per kWh. The spread from the lowest row to the highest is 44×, and it is entirely the model, the GPU and the load; the grid multiplies all of them alike.

*Reporting*

## Which line it goes on

For GPUs you run in Hong Kong, the electricity is your own consumption: it goes into your ESRS E1-5 energy total and its emissions into E1-6 as Scope 2, location-based, which is the method this page's figure matches. The market-based figure nets your contracted supply and needs your own contracts. Tokens bought from a hosted API are the provider's Scope 2 and your Scope 3 category 1, and sit outside your E1-5 line; [the why page](https://leadgreen.ai/why/#hosted) lists what to ask the provider. Ember's figure is a lifecycle intensity for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported.

# Taiwan: the carbon of AI inference per billion tokens

> About 40.3 kg CO2e per billion LLM output tokens (40.3 g per million) on Taiwan's grid (635 gCO2e/kWh, 2024, Ember), every index model priced.

> Lead Green, a Katonic project. Canonical page: https://leadgreen.ai/grids/taiwan/ (this file: https://leadgreen.ai/grids/taiwan/index.md). Updated 19 October 2026, data version 2026-10-19. Licence: CC BY 4.0 for the compilation and text; sources keep their own licences. GPU energy only, measured at steady state on a busy server (the most energy-efficient configuration under a latency limit). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted. Every figure is a floor; a lightly used server sits well above it. Machine-readable data: https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/ (see llms.txt).

*[Grids](https://leadgreen.ai/grids/) · Asia · a market Katonic sells in or expects to*

An LLM served on Taiwan's grid emits about **40.3 kg CO2e per billion output tokens**, 40.3 g per million, at the index's reference row (Qwen 3 32B, 2 × H100, 63.5 Wh/M), GPU energy only; the index's lowest row emits 8.2 kg and its highest 363.9 kg. The grid ran at **635 gCO2e per kWh** in 2024 on Ember's yearly figures, 1.3× the world average of 473, and 156th of the 193 countries Ember covers, counting from the cleanest. Energy per token does not change with geography; carbon per token does.

Carbon per token is energy per token times the grid. The energy figures here are GPU-only floors from a busy server; a lightly loaded deployment sits above them, and so does anything that includes the host, the network and the cooling. Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000 gives kg CO2e per billion output tokens.

*Trend*

## Taiwan's grid, year by year

From 2023 to 2025 the intensity fell 2 percent, from 644.5 to 633.6 gCO2e per kWh. The table uses 2024, the latest year with a value for every listed grid; on the 2025 figure the reference row would carry 40.2 kg per billion tokens.

*Ember yearly emissions intensity for Taiwan, and the reference row priced on each year*

| Year | g CO2e per kWh | kg CO2e per billion tokens, reference row |
|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 644.5 | 40.9 |
| 2024 | 635.2 | 40.3 |
| 2025 | 633.6 | 40.2 |

Lifecycle emissions intensity: CO2e per kWh of net generation, built from per-technology lifecycle factors (IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III midpoints, all gases at GWP-100), so upstream methane, supply chains and plant manufacture are included. Production-based: imports and grid losses are excluded. A location-based figure for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported. A GPU server draws much the same power around the clock, while an annual average weights each hour by its generation, so on a grid whose clean supply peaks at midday a flat load sees a higher figure than the average.

*Reporting*

## Which line it goes on

For GPUs you run in Taiwan, the electricity is your own consumption: it goes into your ESRS E1-5 energy total and its emissions into E1-6 as Scope 2, location-based, which is the method this page's figure matches. The market-based figure nets your contracted supply and needs your own contracts. Tokens bought from a hosted API are the provider's Scope 2 and your Scope 3 category 1, and sit outside your E1-5 line; [the why page](https://leadgreen.ai/why/#hosted) lists what to ask the provider. Ember's figure is a lifecycle intensity for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported.

*Questions*

## Asked about AI carbon in Taiwan

### What is the grid carbon intensity of Taiwan?

635 gCO2e per kWh in 2024, on Ember's yearly electricity data: a lifecycle, location-based figure for the country's own generation, 1.3× the world average of 473. Ember's 2025 figure is 633.6.

### How much CO2 does a million AI tokens produce in Taiwan?

At the index's reference row (Qwen 3 32B on 2 × H100, 63.5 Wh per million output tokens, GPU only), about 40.3 grams of CO2e per million tokens, or 40.3 kg per billion, on Taiwan's 2024 grid. Across the index the range is 8.2 to 363.9 kg per billion tokens. A lightly loaded server sits above these floors, and host, network and cooling are not counted.

### Is running AI in Taiwan cleaner than the world average?

Taiwan's 2024 intensity of 635 gCO2e per kWh is 1.3× the world average of 473 (473 gCO2e per kWh). The same tokens on the same GPUs produce the same energy figure anywhere; only the carbon figure moves with the grid.

### Can I use this figure for my Scope 2 report in Taiwan?

As a comparison, not as a filing. Ember's intensity is a lifecycle figure on net generation, not a Scope 2 combustion factor, and it is location-based; a market-based figure needs your own contracted supply. Tokens bought from a hosted API land in your Scope 3 category 1, not your Scope 2. The why page explains both.

### Where do these figures come from?

Grid intensity: Ember, Yearly electricity data, October 2026 release (2024; 2023, 2024, 2025 shown), CC BY 4.0, retrieved 17 October 2026. Energy per token: the ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (data compiled 16 February 2026). Carbon is Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000.

## Where every figure came from

Grid intensity: [Ember, Yearly electricity data](https://ember-energy.org/data/yearly-electricity-data/), October 2026 release, emissions intensity of total generation, 2023, 2024, 2025 (CC BY 4.0), retrieved 17 October 2026. Energy per token: [ML.ENERGY Leaderboard](https://ml.energy/leaderboard/) version 3.0 (released 1 December 2025; data compiled 16 February 2026; retrieved 26 September 2026), The ML.ENERGY Initiative, started at SymbioticLab, University of Michigan. Text Conversation task, 328 stable configurations. Energy per token is steady-state GPU energy divided by the output tokens generated in the window, measured with Zeus under vLLM 0.11.1 on H100 80GB HBM3 and B200 servers; energy per request is that figure times the average output length. Each index row is the lowest-energy configuration for its model and GPU at or under a 500 ms median inter-token latency, the leaderboard's own default ceiling, which no configuration reaches. Apache 2.0 per the [ml-energy/benchmark-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ml-energy/benchmark-v3) dataset card. Cite [Chung et al., The ML.ENERGY Benchmark, NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06371).

Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000 gives kg CO2e per billion output tokens.

*Trend*

## Qatar's grid, year by year

From 2023 to 2025 the intensity was flat at about 581.9 gCO2e per kWh. The table uses 2024, the latest year with a value for every listed grid; on the 2025 figure the reference row would carry 36.9 kg per billion tokens.

*Ember yearly emissions intensity for Qatar, and the reference row priced on each year*

| Year | g CO2e per kWh | kg CO2e per billion tokens, reference row |
|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 584.2 | 37.1 |
| 2024 | 581.7 | 36.9 |
| 2025 | 581.9 | 36.9 |

Lifecycle emissions intensity: CO2e per kWh of net generation, built from per-technology lifecycle factors (IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III midpoints, all gases at GWP-100), so upstream methane, supply chains and plant manufacture are included. Production-based: imports and grid losses are excluded. A location-based figure for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported. A GPU server draws much the same power around the clock, while an annual average weights each hour by its generation, so on a grid whose clean supply peaks at midday a flat load sees a higher figure than the average.

*Every model*

*Reporting*

## Which line it goes on

For GPUs you run in Qatar, the electricity is your own consumption: it goes into your ESRS E1-5 energy total and its emissions into E1-6 as Scope 2, location-based, which is the method this page's figure matches. The market-based figure nets your contracted supply and needs your own contracts. Tokens bought from a hosted API are the provider's Scope 2 and your Scope 3 category 1, and sit outside your E1-5 line; [the why page](https://leadgreen.ai/why/#hosted) lists what to ask the provider. Ember's figure is a lifecycle intensity for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported.

*Questions*

## Asked about AI carbon in Qatar

### What is the grid carbon intensity of Qatar?

582 gCO2e per kWh in 2024, on Ember's yearly electricity data: a lifecycle, location-based figure for the country's own generation, 1.2× the world average of 473. Ember's 2025 figure is 581.9.

### How much CO2 does a million AI tokens produce in Qatar?

At the index's reference row (Qwen 3 32B on 2 × H100, 63.5 Wh per million output tokens, GPU only), about 36.9 grams of CO2e per million tokens, or 36.9 kg per billion, on Qatar's 2024 grid. Across the index the range is 7.5 to 333.3 kg per billion tokens. A lightly loaded server sits above these floors, and host, network and cooling are not counted.

### Is running AI in Qatar cleaner than the world average?

Qatar's 2024 intensity of 582 gCO2e per kWh is 1.2× the world average of 473 (473 gCO2e per kWh). The same tokens on the same GPUs produce the same energy figure anywhere; only the carbon figure moves with the grid.

### Can I use this figure for my Scope 2 report in Qatar?

As a comparison, not as a filing. Ember's intensity is a lifecycle figure on net generation, not a Scope 2 combustion factor, and it is location-based; a market-based figure needs your own contracted supply. Tokens bought from a hosted API land in your Scope 3 category 1, not your Scope 2. The why page explains both.

### Where do these figures come from?

Grid intensity: Ember, Yearly electricity data, October 2026 release (2024; 2023, 2024, 2025 shown), CC BY 4.0, retrieved 17 October 2026. Energy per token: the ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (data compiled 16 February 2026). Carbon is Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000.

*Sources*

## Where every figure came from

Grid intensity: [Ember, Yearly electricity data](https://ember-energy.org/data/yearly-electricity-data/), October 2026 release, emissions intensity of total generation, 2023, 2024, 2025 (CC BY 4.0), retrieved 17 October 2026. Energy per token: [ML.ENERGY Leaderboard](https://ml.energy/leaderboard/) version 3.0 (released 1 December 2025; data compiled 16 February 2026; retrieved 26 September 2026), The ML.ENERGY Initiative, started at SymbioticLab, University of Michigan. Text Conversation task, 328 stable configurations. Energy per token is steady-state GPU energy divided by the output tokens generated in the window, measured with Zeus under vLLM 0.11.1 on H100 80GB HBM3 and B200 servers; energy per request is that figure times the average output length. Each index row is the lowest-energy configuration for its model and GPU at or under a 500 ms median inter-token latency, the leaderboard's own default ceiling, which no configuration reaches. Apache 2.0 per the [ml-energy/benchmark-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ml-energy/benchmark-v3) dataset card. Cite [Chung et al., The ML.ENERGY Benchmark, NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06371).

*Reporting*

## Which line it goes on

For GPUs you run in Singapore, the electricity is your own consumption: it goes into your ESRS E1-5 energy total and its emissions into E1-6 as Scope 2, location-based, which is the method this page's figure matches. The market-based figure nets your contracted supply and needs your own contracts. Tokens bought from a hosted API are the provider's Scope 2 and your Scope 3 category 1, and sit outside your E1-5 line; [the why page](https://leadgreen.ai/why/#hosted) lists what to ask the provider. Ember's figure is a lifecycle intensity for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported.

*Questions*

## Asked about AI carbon in Singapore

### What is the grid carbon intensity of Singapore?

499 gCO2e per kWh in 2024, on Ember's yearly electricity data: a lifecycle, location-based figure for the country's own generation, 1.1× the world average of 473. Ember's 2025 figure is 497.0.

### How much CO2 does a million AI tokens produce in Singapore?

At the index's reference row (Qwen 3 32B on 2 × H100, 63.5 Wh per million output tokens, GPU only), about 31.6 grams of CO2e per million tokens, or 31.6 kg per billion, on Singapore's 2024 grid. Across the index the range is 6.5 to 285.7 kg per billion tokens. A lightly loaded server sits above these floors, and host, network and cooling are not counted.

### Is running AI in Singapore cleaner than the world average?

Singapore's 2024 intensity of 499 gCO2e per kWh is 1.1× the world average of 473 (473 gCO2e per kWh). The same tokens on the same GPUs produce the same energy figure anywhere; only the carbon figure moves with the grid.

### Can I use this figure for my Scope 2 report in Singapore?

As a comparison, not as a filing. Ember's intensity is a lifecycle figure on net generation, not a Scope 2 combustion factor, and it is location-based; a market-based figure needs your own contracted supply. Tokens bought from a hosted API land in your Scope 3 category 1, not your Scope 2. The why page explains both.

### Where do these figures come from?

Grid intensity: Ember, Yearly electricity data, October 2026 release (2024; 2023, 2024, 2025 shown), CC BY 4.0, retrieved 17 October 2026. Energy per token: the ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (data compiled 16 February 2026). Carbon is Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000.

*Sources*

## Where every figure came from

Grid intensity: [Ember, Yearly electricity data](https://ember-energy.org/data/yearly-electricity-data/), October 2026 release, emissions intensity of total generation, 2023, 2024, 2025 (CC BY 4.0), retrieved 17 October 2026. Energy per token: [ML.ENERGY Leaderboard](https://ml.energy/leaderboard/) version 3.0 (released 1 December 2025; data compiled 16 February 2026; retrieved 26 September 2026), The ML.ENERGY Initiative, started at SymbioticLab, University of Michigan. Text Conversation task, 328 stable configurations. Energy per token is steady-state GPU energy divided by the output tokens generated in the window, measured with Zeus under vLLM 0.11.1 on H100 80GB HBM3 and B200 servers; energy per request is that figure times the average output length. Each index row is the lowest-energy configuration for its model and GPU at or under a 500 ms median inter-token latency, the leaderboard's own default ceiling, which no configuration reaches. Apache 2.0 per the [ml-energy/benchmark-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ml-energy/benchmark-v3) dataset card. Cite [Chung et al., The ML.ENERGY Benchmark, NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06371).

Licensed [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), offered as-is and without warranty; state whether you changed any rows or columns. Underlying data: ML.ENERGY Leaderboard v3.0 (The ML.ENERGY Initiative; Apache 2.0 per the ml-energy/benchmark-v3 dataset card; cite Chung et al., The ML.ENERGY Benchmark, NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks, arXiv 2505.06371); Ember, Yearly electricity data, October 2026 release (CC BY 4.0); AI Energy Score (Apache-2.0 as tagged on its Space; results reproduced as facts with attribution); NVIDIA figures reproduced as facts from the documents named in the sources ledger.

# Japan: the carbon of AI inference per billion tokens

> About 30.7 kg CO2e per billion LLM output tokens (30.7 g per million) on Japan's grid (484 gCO2e/kWh, 2024, Ember), every index model priced.
>
> Lead Green, a Katonic project. Canonical page: https://leadgreen.ai/grids/japan/ (this file: https://leadgreen.ai/grids/japan/index.md). Updated 19 October 2026, data version 2026-10-19. Licence: CC BY 4.0 for the compilation and text; sources keep their own licences. GPU energy only, measured at steady state on a busy server (the most energy-efficient configuration under a latency limit). Host, network, cooling and idle time are not counted. Every figure is a floor; a lightly used server sits well above it. Machine-readable data: https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/ (see llms.txt).

*[Grids](https://leadgreen.ai/grids/) · Asia · a reference grid*

An LLM served on Japan's grid emits about **30.7 kg CO2e per billion output tokens**, 30.7 g per million, at the index's reference row (Qwen 3 32B, 2 × H100, 63.5 Wh/M), GPU energy only; the index's lowest row emits 6.3 kg and its highest 277.5 kg. The grid ran at **484 gCO2e per kWh** in 2024 on Ember's yearly figures, close to the world average of 473, and 101st of the 193 countries Ember covers, counting from the cleanest. Energy per token does not change with geography; carbon per token does.

**Area** Japan (JPN, JP). **Basis** lifecycle, location-based, annual average. **Data** [grid.json](https://leadgreen.ai/api/v1/grid.json). Updated 19 October 2026.

Carbon per token is energy per token times the grid. The energy figures here are GPU-only floors from a busy server; a lightly loaded deployment sits above them, and so does anything that includes the host, the network and the cooling. Wh/M × gCO2e per kWh ÷ 1,000 gives kg CO2e per billion output tokens.

*Trend*

## Japan's grid, year by year

From 2023 to 2025 the intensity fell 4 percent, from 492.6 to 473.7 gCO2e per kWh. The table uses 2024, the latest year with a value for every listed grid; on the 2025 figure the reference row would carry 30.1 kg per billion tokens.

*Ember yearly emissions intensity for Japan, and the reference row priced on each year*

| Year | g CO2e per kWh | kg CO2e per billion tokens, reference row |
|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 492.6 | 31.3 |
| 2024 | 484.3 | 30.7 |
| 2025 | 473.7 | 30.1 |

Lifecycle emissions intensity: CO2e per kWh of net generation, built from per-technology lifecycle factors (IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III midpoints, all gases at GWP-100), so upstream methane, supply chains and plant manufacture are included. Production-based: imports and grid losses are excluded. A location-based figure for comparing places, not a Scope 2 combustion factor to file as reported. A GPU server draws much the same power around the clock, while an annual average weights each hour by its generation, so on a grid whose clean supply peaks at midday a flat load sees a higher figure than the average.
